takeaway: You don't need a stress-free life. Start with one tool that fits, notice what it helps with, and build from there.
why: Understand why stress belongs in the recovery conversation, then try one tool you can use between appointments.

slides.title: When life is demanding
slides.content: You may notice that you hold more tension, sleep differently, or find familiar symptoms harder to manage during a demanding week. Stress can be part of that picture. It does not mean your pain is imagined or that stress explains everything.

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.content: Stress can affect attention, sleep, muscle tension, and how you respond to discomfort. Pain can add to stress too. That is why we look at both what your body is being asked to do and what else is happening in your life.

slides.title: You don't need a stress-free life
slides.content: The aim is to have ways to respond when things feel demanding. You can work on movement, daily routines, and stress together. You do not need to get one perfect before the others can help.

slides.title: Try comfortable breathing
slides.content: Sit comfortably with your feet supported. Let your breath come in gently through your nose and out through your mouth if comfortable. Keep an easy rhythm; there is no need to force a deep breath or hold it. Start with a few comfortable breaths. Stop if you feel dizzy, distressed, or unwell.

slides.title: Pick one tool
slides.content: If breathing is not for you, try a brief comfortable walk, a quiet break, or speaking with someone supportive. You don't need to do all three. Pick the one that resonates with you and try to make it part of your daily routine.

slides.title: Notice what it helps with
slides.content: Did you feel a little steadier? Was it easier to choose your next step? Did nothing change? All are useful observations. A calming tool does not have to remove pain to be useful. We'll continue building your toolbox.

title: When stress adds to the picture
